The impression I got was basically the black tar from Star Trek TNG that killed Tasha Yar like a redshirt.

Also:

it is extremely difficult to change the subject when communicating with a face of SCP-830.

Difficult for who? Given how some Foundation personnel in these early articles treat D-Class and even civilians, I find it hard to believe they couldn't find plenty of sociopathic people to communicate with SCP-830.

Aside from that, it's not a matter of inconsistency that bothers me, it's the matter of "group uniformity", a tremendous problem that Harry Turtledove and Star Trek Voyager in particular have—when a writer depicts an entire group of people or even the entire human species as being explicitly one way or in total agreement with the designated leader and this is treated as normal.

item.content:encoded:
I find this pretty boring. As far as I can tell, the CI used this pit to kill/torture people for information maybe… So what? Why should I care about the Order of the Black Box when I know nothing about them?

It's a pit of souls. That's it. It's not bringing anything new to the table, it's not interesting, and I can't find a narrative in it that isn't overly downplayed. So many things have done this concept before, and this has next to nothing distinguishing it from everything else like it.

What confuses me though, is that you spend a good bit of the article saying that we can talk to people in there, but nothing good ever comes out of it. That feels like such a tease, because that could have led somewhere interesting. You could have told us about the cultists in there or the origins of the pit or something.

I really don't see why this deserved praise. If this was the first SCP I read, I'd probably think 'Meh… Wait, there are over 2000 of these?… Why?'. That's not good. Sorry, but -1.
